thread:
maya: Hey — doing an nsys run against the private runtime binary and almost all CUDA/kernel frames show up as [unknown] or raw addresses. Kernel timelines are useful but no source/line info. Anyone seen this with distroless images + CUPTI?

nick: Can you paste the exact nsys command + docker run you used? :thinking_face:

maya: Sure, snippet:```
docker run --rm --entrypoint=/bin/sh my-image -c './serve_bin'
nsys profile --output=serve_trace --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --sample=cpu -- ./run_prof.sh
```
I also ran readelf -n on the binary and the build-id is "0xabcdef1234..." but /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/ab/cdef... doesn't exist inside the image.

sam: Are we stripping debug symbols at package time? Distroless images often copy only the stripped binary.

maya: Packaging step contains `strip -s /out/serve_bin` in the Dockerfile (we do a two-stage build). I thought -g at compile would be enough.

jules: Strip -s removes symbol table. Typical workflow: keep full debug in a separate .debug file via `objcopy --only-keep-debug` and place it under /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/<id>. That lets profilers resolve lines while reducing runtime size.

maya: I tried placing the .debug file under /usr/lib/debug in the image, still got unknowns. The nsys UI logs show: "no lineinfo: buildid mismatch for /workspace/serve_bin -> expected 0xabcdef... got 0x123456..."

nick: That suggests the binary you built and the binary you profiled are different (build-id mismatch). Could the container be running a different binary than the one you built (shadowed by a host mount or stale layer)?

maya: The image is built by CI, tag -> local pull. I reproduced locally by bind-mounting the debug dir: `-v /tmp/debug:/usr/lib/debug:ro` and then the trace resolved lines. So bind-mounting fixed it.

perf-bot: NOTE: CI change CL #4578 (2026-03-12) added a final `strip -s` step into packaging stage for smaller images.

sam: Two possibilities: 1) The build-id inside the binary isn't matching the debug file path (maybe objcopy changed it), or 2) CUPTI/LD_PRELOAD and different libc in container cause nsys symbol resolving to consult host paths or different mappings.

maya: I also saw CUPTI warning in the nsys log: `CUPTI: unable to find address->symbol mapping for 0x7f8c...`. And the recorded auxv in the trace shows AT_SYSINFO_EHDR pointing to a vDSO address that doesn't exist in the container mount. Maybe the profiler is resolving vDSO/ld.so based on host layout.

jules: For perf/perfetto you can use a symfs root (e.g., `perf record --symfs /path/to/debugroot ...`) so it looks up symbols under that tree. nsys historically expects debug files to be discoverable in the same root as the recorded file paths. If our build path was /workspace/..., the debug tree must replicate that under /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/... or you need to remap with --symfs-like option.

nick: Also confirm we didn't compressed or change build-ids via strip/objcopy options. run: `readelf -n ./serve_bin | grep Build` and `sha1sum` the elf sections. Compare against /usr/lib/debug/.build-id file name.

maya: ran `readelf -n` inside container: Build ID : 0xabcdef1234. Then `ls /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/ab/cdef1234.debug` -> file exists when bind-mounted. But without bind-mount the file is missing. So the packaging step omitted it.

sam: Packaging fix is straightforward. But there's a second flaky bit: CUPTI adds a shim and sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH, which can make the loader pick a different libc from the host if LD paths are wrong when running nsys from outside the container and profiling into the container. We had a wrapper script that sets `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH; exec "$@"` — that can cause symbol mismatches if the loaded libc and binary were built against different glibc versions.

maya: Good call — our wrapper was introduced in 2025 to force CUDA libs. I removed LD_LIBRARY_PATH override and used patchelf to set RUNPATH at build time; that also fixed a spurious "unresolved symbol libc_start_main" in some traces.

infra-bot: FYI we have a helper in eng-runtime: `/scripts/profiler/symfix.sh` that can generate the .debug tree and compute build-id paths. It runs `eu-strip --only-keep-debug` + `objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink`.

jules: Long term: (1) change CI to produce split debug packages and install into /usr/lib/debug inside the image (or upload to debug server and mount during profiling), (2) add an integration test that runs nsys inside a containerized environment and asserts that top-20 CUDA kernels have filename:line info, (3) document known CUPTI caveats (LD_PRELOAD/LD_LIBRARY_PATH) in eng-runtime debugging doc.

maya: I'll open a PR to revert the strip step in packaging, add split debug, and wire the symfix helper into the release job. Plan also includes a small KB in eng-runtime/README about "How to make nsys show lines in distroless containers".

nick: One more trick: when you can't modify the image, you can run a helper container that mounts the image's FS and places debug files at the expected /usr/lib/debug path, then run nsys from that helper container with `--containerized` flags so symbol resolution sees the debug files.

maya: Thanks — binder trick + removing LD_LIBRARY_PATH override + adding split debug fixed my traces locally. Will post PR + repro instructions. :+1:

perf-bot: automated note: created issue ENGRT-1123 "CI: produce split-debug artifacts for runtime images" from this thread.
